audit.why: TRICKY reflects Yasuo's carry ceiling rather than the lane itself, and the lane phase is genuinely Lillia's — 66.67% over 24 games, and every content why from Level 2 to first item is hers. Left the enum alone but flagged the tension.

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 3, 4-5 and first item were credited to Yasuo, and Level 1 to Lillia, both the opposite of the whys on those rows.
audit.why: whys[0] 'You're weak at level 1 with only Q, but so is melee Yasuo' — a wash. whys[2], whys[3] and whys[5] are all Lillia windows ('your best lane window to grind him down', 'your skirmish power outpaces his pre-crit'). Packet levelChart reads Skill, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Yasuo.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 aligned in both layers with matching ratings, as one group. Rows 4 and 6 already agreed.
sources: content whys[0], whys[2], whys[3], whys[5], spikes[1]

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer describes Wind Wall only as 'blocks every projectile' without naming what of yours it blocks, gives no cooldown, and never mentions the two facts that decide the kite: Sweeping Blade cannot re-dash the same target, and Last Breath requires an airborne enemy.
audit.why: Lillia's E Swirlseed is flagged projectile in her own kit, and Wind Wall is flagged blocksProjectiles: 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds', 25/23/21/19/17s. Sweeping Blade: 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds' — he must chain through minions to reach you, so denying minions denies the gap-close. Last Breath: 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion' on 70/50/30s, and Steel Tempest only knocks airborne at 2 stacks of Gathering Storm, which is the visible tell. Her Q and W are not projectiles and go through the wall.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall named as the answer to Swirlseed specifically with its 17-25s cooldown and 4s duration; the no-re-dash rule and the airborne prerequisite for his R now stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'hold your poke until it is spent' never said how long spent lasts.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 — a huge window in a lane built on E-slow into Q sweetspot.
audit.corrected: 25s at rank 1 stated in dosFull[0].d and the full range in breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: Q's outer ring on his last-hits plus the passive speed means he literally cannot touch you at level 1.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you have only Q, and he is a melee who has to walk into the minions to farm.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Count it out loud if you must. - Your passive move speed has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Wind Wall: 25/23/21/19/17s, four seconds of blocking every projectile — your E seed included, so bait it before you throw. - Sweeping Blade cannot re-dash the same target, so he needs minions to chain onto you. - Last Breath, 70/50/30s, needs an airborne target.

edits.before: Track Yasuo’s Wind Wall: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Wind Wall, 17-25s and four seconds long, eats your E seed outright — bait it, then throw. Last Breath needs a knock-up first: no airborne target, no ult.

edits.before: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 and swallows Swirlseed whole — fake the throw, and send the real one once W is gone.

edits.before: Yasuo spends Wind Wall early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade cannot re-dash the same target — deny him minions and he stalls.

edits.before: That’s Yasuo’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: His Q knocks up only at 2 stacks — that is the tell before Last Breath.

edits.before: Pop Windwall to block your E seed and eat your wind-up, then E-dash onto you while it's up
edits.after: Pop Wind Wall to swallow your E seed for a full 4s, then E-dash off a minion onto you

notes: Worth a human decision: this page is labelled TRICKY at 7/10 difficulty with a 66.67% win rate over 24 games and a level chart that is now Lillia's from 2 through first item. The difficulty enum may be a champion-wide default rather than a judgement about Yasuo — I did not change it. Lillia's Q and W are not projectiles in the kit data, so Wind Wall does not stop them; the page never said otherwise, but it also never told the player they can still Q through the wall.
